listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a music appreciation class.

Most wind instruments, which are played by blowing into them, went through lots of modifications before becoming the standardized instruments we see and hear today. Now, most brass instruments, like the trumpet and trombone, underwent many centuries of refinement before being standardized. But the tuba only took about 180 years to reach its current form. That's because through centuries, composers and inventors wanted an ideal bass instrument to play those really low notes. Rather than tinker with an instrument they didn't love, they would discard it and start again. So the tuba doesn't really have a clear ancestor — more a series of unrelated precursors trying to do what it now does.

An early example was the serpent. The serpent was made of a wooden tube bent into the shape of, well, a serpent — or the letter S. The problem was, it didn't sound great. The wooden tube was too wide, which caused problems with intonation, meaning it was hard to hit the right notes. Imagine a choir of voices accompanied by a serpent booming along out of tune. Ouch.

Well, so long, serpent. And hello, ophicleide. The ophicleide's main advantage was that it was made of brass. The brass construction made its intonation much better. The ophicleide became much more popular than the serpent. The composer Berlioz used it in some famous pieces, but still the ophicleide wasn't the answer. Its pitch range was pretty narrow, and composers wanted something that could play lower notes.

早期例子是蛇形号。蛇形号由弯成——嗯——蛇形或字母 S 形的木管制成。问题是声音不好。木管太粗，造成音准问题，意思是很难奏准音。想象一群人声合唱，配上蛇形号走调地轰鸣。哎哟。

多数管乐器——靠吹奏演奏——在成为我们今天所见所听的标准化乐器前经历了大量改动。多数铜管乐器，如小号与长号，标准化前经历了数世纪的改进。但大号只花了大约一百八十年就达到现今形态。那是因为数世纪里，作曲家与发明家想要一种理想的低音乐器来演奏那些很低的音。与其修补他们不喜欢的乐器，他们会弃之重来。所以大号其实没有清晰祖先——更多是一系列无关前身，试图做它现在做的事。

早期例子是蛇形号。蛇形号由弯成——嗯——蛇形或字母 S 形的木管制成。问题是声音不好。木管太粗，造成音准问题，意思是很难奏准音。想象一群人声合唱，配上蛇形号走调地轰鸣。哎哟。

好，再见蛇形号。你好，奥菲克莱德号。奥菲克莱德号的主要优势是用铜制成。铜制结构使其音准好得多。奥菲克莱德号比蛇形号流行得多。作曲家柏辽兹在一些名曲中用过它，但奥菲克莱德号仍不是答案。其音域相当窄，作曲家想要能奏更低音的东西。

speaking.prompt: Thank you for participating. I'd like to learn about your experiences with books and reading. Was there a time in your life when you read more or less than you do now? What changed?

content.promptText: Thank you for participating. I'd like to learn about your experiences with books and reading. Was there a time in your life when you read more or less than you do now? What changed?

speaking.answer: Yes, actually. When I was in middle school, I read a lot more than I do now. I'd finish a novel almost every week, usually adventure or fantasy stories, because I loved escaping into another world. Uh, then in high school my schedule got really busy with homework and exams, and I stopped reading for fun. Also, my phone became a big distraction, so in my free time I'd scroll through videos instead. I really miss that old habit, though, because books made me feel calm. Lately I've been trying to read for twenty minutes before bed, and it's helping me relax. So the main change was my time and my attention, and now I'm slowly bringing books back into my life.

speaking.prompt: Great. In your opinion, is reading for pleasure a popular way people spend their free time where you live? Why do you think that is?

content.promptText: Great. In your opinion, is reading for pleasure a popular way people spend their free time where you live? Why do you think that is?

speaking.answer: Hmm, I'd say it's not very popular, at least among young people where I live. Most of my friends spend their free time on their phones, watching short videos or playing games. Those things are fast and easy, you know, while a book needs patience and quiet time. Also, people are really busy with school and work, so by the evening they just want something simple to relax. That said, some people still really love reading, and bookstores and libraries do get busy on weekends. Older people especially seem to enjoy it more, since they have more quiet time at home. So I think reading is still respected, but it's not a top choice anymore, mostly because screens are so convenient and entertaining.
speaking.translation: 很好。在你看来，你所在的地方，阅读是人们消遣时光的流行方式吗？你认为这是为什么？

context.text: You have signed up for a study run by a university research group that is investigating people's experiences with books and reading. You will have a short online interview with me. I will ask you some questions. From this point on, the questions will not appear on screen, so please listen carefully.

speaking.prompt: Interesting. Do you think reading different types of books helps people understand each other and get along better? Why or why not?
speaking.promptZh: 有意思。你认为阅读不同类型的书籍有助于人们相互理解并更好地相处吗？为什么？

content.promptText: Interesting. Do you think reading different types of books helps people understand each other and get along better? Why or why not?

speaking.answer: I think it does, yes. When you read a story about someone from another country or background, you start to see how they think and feel. Um, I once read a novel about a family who moved to a new country, and it made me realize how lonely and confusing that can be. After that, I was kinder and more patient with the new students at my school, and I tried to include them. Different books, like history or science, also show you that people have different experiences. It's hard to judge someone when you've already seen the world through their eyes. Of course, reading alone won't fix every conflict. But I believe it builds empathy, and empathy helps people get along much better.
speaking.translation: 有意思。你认为阅读不同类型的书籍有助于人们相互理解并更好地相处吗？为什么？

speaking.prompt: Good points. Looking ahead, some people believe that future generations will read less than today's generation. Do you agree or disagree? Why?

content.promptText: Good points. Looking ahead, some people believe that future generations will read less than today's generation. Do you agree or disagree? Why?

speaking.answer: I partly agree, honestly. Future generations will probably read fewer traditional books, because technology keeps giving them faster entertainment. Uh, even now, kids grow up with tablets and short videos, so sitting with a long book feels much harder for them. But I don't think reading will disappear. People will just read in different ways, like on their phones, in articles, or through audiobooks. I mean, those still count as reading and listening to words. And schools will probably keep encouraging it, because it's so important for learning and for building thinking skills. So I'd say they'll read less long, deep material than we do, but they'll still read every day. The format will change, but the habit will survive in some form.

To: Maria
Subject: Request for Lecture Notes

writing.answer:
Dear Maria,

I am writing to ask for a favor. I missed today's biology lecture because I was unwell and had to stay home to rest.

I am worried about falling behind, so I was hoping you could share your notes and let me know about any important announcements or assignments I missed. If you have some free time this week, it would be a huge help to go over the material together.

Thank you so much in advance for your kindness. I really appreciate it and would be glad to return the favor.

Sincerely,
A classmate

content.post: Paul: I believe advertisements mainly manipulate consumer choices. They often create unrealistic expectations and encourage materialism, leading people to buy things they don't need and fostering a culture of overconsumption.

writing.answer: In my opinion, advertising mainly influences consumers in negative ways, though it does provide some useful information. I understand Claire's view that ads inform people about new products and help them make purchasing decisions, which can support local businesses and the wider economy. That informative role is real and valuable. However, I agree more with Paul that many advertisements create unrealistic expectations and encourage materialism. I remember a smartphone ad that made me feel my perfectly working phone was outdated, and I almost bought a new one I did not need at all. Reflecting on it, the impact was clearly negative, because it manipulated my emotions rather than addressing any genuine need. Therefore, I believe advertising should be regulated for honesty, so its informative benefits remain while its tendency to push overconsumption and dissatisfaction is reduced. Used responsibly, advertising can inform without pressuring people into wasteful choices.

Paul：我相信广告主要操纵消费者的选择。它们常常制造不切实际的期望并鼓励物质主义，导致人们购买不需要的东西，并助长过度消费的文化。

reading.prompt: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
reading.passage: Crop rotation is a farming technique that involves growing a series of different types of crops in the same area across a sequence of seasons. Different crops use different nutrients from the soil, so rotating them prevents the soil from becoming depleted. [1] Th__ method [2] he___ to [3] red___ pests [4] a__ diseases; [5] i_ also [6] decr_____ the [7] ne__ for [8] chem____ fertilizers, [9] prom_____ sustainable [10] agric______. Farmers use this practice to improve crop yields and maintain healthy soil.

content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: Crop rotation is a farming technique that involves growing a series of different types of crops in the same area across a sequence of seasons. Different crops use different nutrients from the soil, so rotating them prevents the soil from becoming depleted. [1] Th__ method [2] he___ to [3] red___ pests [4] a__ diseases; [5] i_ also [6] decr_____ the [7] ne__ for [8] chem____ fertilizers, [9] prom_____ sustainable [10] agric______. Farmers use this practice to improve crop yields and maintain healthy soil.

reading.answer:
1. is → This
2. lps → helps
3. uce → reduce
4. nd → and
5. t → it
6. eases → decreases
7. ed → need
8. ical → chemical
9. oting → promoting
10. ulture → agriculture
reading.explanation: 1. 空前有“Th”，空后“method”是单数名词，这里指代前文的“Crop rotation”，需用 This 表示“这种方法”。 2. 空前“he”提示动词以h开头，主语“This method”是单数，helps to do sth. 表示“有助于做某事”。 3. 空前“red”提示单词以re-开头，与宾语“pests and diseases”搭配，reduce 表示“减少”，是此语境下的核心动词。 4. 空前“a”和空后“diseases”提示连接词，“pests and diseases”（害虫与疾病）是农业文本中的固定并列短语。 5. 空前“i”和空后“also”提示代词，it 指代前文的轮作方法，作本句主语，表示“它（轮作）也……”。 6. 空前“decr”提示单词以decr-开头，主语是单数it，decreases 与“the need for”搭配，表示“减少对……的需求”。 7. 空前“ne”和空后“for”提示名词，need for sth. 表示“对某物的需要”，与 decrease 搭配符合句意。 8. 空前“chem”提示形容词 chemical，修饰 fertilizers（化肥），构成“化学肥料”这一常见术语，呼应可持续农业主题。 9. 空前“prom”提示单词以prom-开头，此处用现在分词作状语，表示“从而促进”，说明轮作带来的积极结果。 10. 空前“agric”提示名词 agriculture，与 sustainable 构成“可持续农业”，这是轮作技术所属的核心领域。
reading.translation: 轮作是一种农作技术，在同一地块按季节序列种植不同类型作物。不同作物从土壤中摄取不同养分，轮作可防止土壤耗竭。这种方法有助于减少病虫害，也降低对化肥的需求，促进可持续农业。农民用这一实践提高产量并维持健康土壤。

reading.prompt: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
reading.passage: Mushrooms are made up of two main parts: the mycelium and the fruiting body. The mycelium [1] i_ long-lived, [2] wh___ the fruiting body [3] app____ only [4] wh__ conditions [5] a__ ideal [6] f__ reproduction ([7] li__ after [8] ra__). Usually [9] under______, the mycelium [10] cons____ of a network of thread-like structures that absorb nutrients from the soil. The fruiting body is above ground and responsible for producing and spreading spores. These spores are released into the air to help the mushroom reproduce.

content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: Mushrooms are made up of two main parts: the mycelium and the fruiting body. The mycelium [1] i_ long-lived, [2] wh___ the fruiting body [3] app____ only [4] wh__ conditions [5] a__ ideal [6] f__ reproduction ([7] li__ after [8] ra__). Usually [9] under______, the mycelium [10] cons____ of a network of thread-like structures that absorb nutrients from the soil. The fruiting body is above ground and responsible for producing and spreading spores. These spores are released into the air to help the mushroom reproduce.

reading.answer:
1. s → is
2. ile → while
3. ears → appears
4. en → when
5. re → are
6. or → for
7. ke → like
8. in → rain
9. ground → underground
10. ists → consists
reading.explanation: 1. 主语'mycelium'是单数，需要系动词'is'来描述其长命的特性。 2. 'while'用于对比两个分句，强调mycelium和fruiting body在存在时间上的不同。 3. 主语'fruiting body'是单数，动词用第三人称单数形式'appears'表示出现的动作。 4. 'when'引导时间状语从句，说明fruiting body只在条件理想时出现。 5. 主语'conditions'是复数，因此用'are'与形容词'ideal'匹配，表示条件理想。 6. 'for'表示目的，'for reproduction'指出了fruiting body产生孢子是为了繁殖。 7. 'like'用于引入例子，这里举例说明'after rain'作为理想条件之一。 8. 'rain'与前面的'after'固定搭配，'after rain'是常见的表示雨后的短语。 9. 'underground'描述mycelium通常的位置，与后文的'above ground'形成对比。 10. 主语'mycelium'是单数，动词用第三人称单数形式'consists'，'consist of'表示由...组成。
reading.translation: 蘑菇由两部分组成：菌丝体与子实体。菌丝体寿命长，而子实体仅在条件适合繁殖时出现（如下雨后）。菌丝体通常在地下，由吸收土壤养分的线状结构网络组成。子实体在地上，负责产生并传播孢子。这些孢子释放到空气中，帮助蘑菇繁殖。

reading.translation:
根据文章，金继体现了哪种哲学视角？

金缮是一种古老的日本艺术，通过凸显而非掩盖裂痕，把破碎陶器变为美的对象。工匠用混有金、银或铂金粉末的漆修复裂缝，制成的作品往往比原件更受珍视。
金缮起源于十五世纪末，体现了侘寂哲学——尊崇不完美与无常。
其启示超越陶瓷：鼓励人们把瑕疵当作生命叙事的一部分，从而启发个人成长与韧性。金缮不把损伤视为失败，而将其重构为转化，在追求完美的世界中象征力量、真实与更新。
今天，世界各地的工作坊与工作室既传授其技艺，也讲授其深刻哲学，让学习者不仅获得艺术技能，也领悟接纳、个性与创造性表达。金缮提醒我们：美在于独特，在于「裂缝」所讲述的故事——这一观念适用于学术生活乃至更广领域。

reading.title: The Mysteries of Opal
reading.prompt: All of the following are mentioned as part of the formation process of opals EXCEPT:
reading.promptZh: 以下所有选项都提到了蛋白石形成过程的一部分，除了哪一项？
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Opal is a unique gemstone, known for its vibrant colors that shift as the stone moves. Unlike most gemstones, which form rigid, repeating crystalline structures, opals are amorphous, meaning they lack a fixed internal shape. This is due to the formation process, where silica-rich water seeps into cracks in rocks deep underground, leaving silica deposits when it evaporates. Tiny silica spheres create the internal structure of opals, and these spheres diffract light, separating it into colors, much like a prism does.

Paragraph 2
The color and brilliance of opals depends on the size and spacing of the silica spheres. Larger spheres produce reds and oranges, while smaller spheres result in blues and greens. Because of Australia's unique geological conditions, it is home to over 90 percent of the world's opals. Opals are also fragile. Their high water content and noncrystalline structure make them prone to cracking when exposed to sudden temperature changes. Modern jewelers use techniques such as laser cutting and humidity-controlled storage to better protect opals.

Paragraph 3
Ancient cultures believed opals had mystical properties and brought good luck. The Romans saw them as a symbol of hope and purity, while the Greeks thought they gave the gift of prophecy.

以下所有选项都提到了蛋白石形成过程的一部分，除了哪一项？

Opal is a unique gemstone, known for its vibrant colors that shift as the stone moves. Modern jewelers use techniques such as laser cutting and humidity-controlled storage to better protect opals.

Paragraph 3
Ancient cultures believed opals had mystical properties and brought good luck. The Romans saw them as a symbol of hope and purity, while the Greeks thought they gave the gift of prophecy.

content.stimulusText: The classical civilizations of ancient Greece and Rome have greatly influenced modern society. In [1] fa__, many [2] o_ their [3] instit______ and [4] id___ continue [5] t_ shape [6] t__ modern [7] wo___. The Greeks, [8] f__ example, [9] ma__ significant [10] contri_______ to architecture, art, philosophy, and government, while the Romans created extensive legal and political systems. reading.answer:
1. ct → fact
2. f → of
3. utions → institutions
4. eas → ideas
5. o → to
6. he → the
7. rld → world
8. or → for
9. de → made
10. butions → contributions
reading.explanation: 1. In fact 是固定短语，表示‘事实上’，所以填 ct 组成 fact。 2. many of their 表示‘他们的许多’，of 是介词，所以填 f 组成 of。 3. institutions 意思是‘制度’，与 ideas 并列，instit 是前缀，所以填 utions。 4. ideas 意思是‘思想’，与 institutions 并列，所以填 eas 组成 ideas。 5. continue to shape 是动词不定式结构，表示‘继续塑造’，所以填 o 组成 to。 6. the modern world 是特指现代世界，需要定冠词 the，所以填 he 组成 the。 7. world 意思是‘世界’，与 modern 搭配，所以填 rld 组成 world。 8. for example 是固定短语，表示‘例如’，所以填 or 组成 for。 9. made 是 make 的过去式，表示‘做出’，与 contributions 搭配，所以填 de 组成 made。 10. contributions 意思是‘贡献’，与 to 搭配表示‘对……的贡献’，所以填 butions。
reading.translation: 古希腊与古罗马的古典文明对现代社会影响巨大。事实上，它们的许多制度与理念继续塑造现代世界。例如，希腊人在建筑、艺术、哲学与政府方面作出重大贡献，而罗马人创建了广泛的法律与政治体系。研习这两个古典文明为西方文化的基础提供洞见，也为理解当代实践与社会提供历史语境。

reading.title: Beyond Philosophy's Borders
reading.prompt: According to the passage, metaphilosophy challenges which of the following basic assumptions of philosophical inquiry?
reading.promptZh: 根据文章，元哲学挑战了哲学探究的以下哪项基本假设？
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Metaphilosophy is a field that looks critically at whether philosophical inquiry can truly transcend cultural and linguistic boundaries. While traditional philosophy often aims to uncover universal truths, metaphilosophy questions whether such truths are even accessible across diverse contexts. Language, far from being a neutral vessel, shapes and limits how ideas are expressed and understood. A concept that resonates deeply in one culture may carry entirely different connotations, or none at all, in another. This raises concerns about the global applicability of philosophical frameworks developed in specific cultural milieus. Are we uncovering truths, or merely reinforcing culturally contingent assumptions?

Paragraph 2
Some insist that despite linguistic and cultural variation, certain philosophical concerns, like suffering, justice, or mortality, are shared across societies, suggesting a basis for universality. Yet even these themes may be interpreted through culturally specific lenses. Metaphilosophy doesn't deny the possibility of cross-cultural dialogue but cautions against assuming it is seamless. It encourages philosophers to examine how their methods and assumptions travel, or fail to, across contexts.

Paragraph 3
Critics worry this reflexivity may stall progress, but others see it as essential for avoiding intellectual overreach. By foregrounding these tensions, metaphilosophy aims not to dilute philosophy's aims, but to sharpen them through greater self-awareness and methodological rigor.

Paragraph 1
Metaphilosophy is a field that looks critically at whether philosophical inquiry can truly transcend cultural and linguistic boundaries. While traditional philosophy often aims to uncover universal truths, metaphilosophy questions whether such truths are even accessible across diverse contexts. Language, far from being a neutral vessel, shapes and limits how ideas are expressed and understood. A concept that resonates deeply in one culture may carry entirely different connotations, or none at all, in another. This raises concerns about the global applicability of philosophical frameworks developed in specific cultural milieus. Are we uncovering truths, or merely reinforcing culturally contingent assumptions?

Paragraph 2
Some insist that despite linguistic and cultural variation, certain philosophical concerns, like suffering, justice, or mortality, are shared across societies, suggesting a basis for universality. Yet even these themes may be interpreted through culturally specific lenses. Metaphilosophy doesn't deny the possibility of cross-cultural dialogue but cautions against assuming it is seamless. It encourages philosophers to examine how their methods and assumptions travel, or fail to, across contexts.

Paragraph 3
Critics worry this reflexivity may stall progress, but others see it as essential for avoiding intellectual overreach. By foregrounding these tensions, metaphilosophy aims not to dilute philosophy's aims, but to sharpen them through greater self-awareness and methodological rigor.

reading.translation:
根据文章，元哲学挑战了哲学探究的以下哪项基本假设？

元哲学批判性地探讨哲学探究能否真正超越文化与语言边界。传统哲学常追求普遍真理，元哲学则质疑此类真理在不同语境中是否可达。语言远非中立容器，它塑造并限制观念的表达与理解。在某一文化中深具共鸣的概念，在另一文化中可能含义全异，甚至不存在。这令人怀疑在特定文化土壤中形成的哲学框架能否全球适用：我们是在揭示真理，还是在强化文化偶然的假定？
有人主张，尽管语言与文化各异，苦难、正义、死亡等哲学关切跨社会共享，为普遍性提供基础。但即便这些主题也可能经文化特定透镜被解读。元哲学并不否定跨文化对话，但提醒勿假定其畅通无阻，并鼓励哲学家审视自身方法与假定如何跨语境旅行，或为何失败。
批评者担心这种反思会阻滞进展，也有人视其为避免智识越界的必要。通过凸显这些张力，元哲学并非稀释哲学目标，而是以更强自我意识与方法严谨性使其更锐利。

choices.labelZh: 它无法评估来自不同传统的思想。

reading.answer: B. It may prevent philosophy from accomplishing its mission.
reading.explanation:
A. 文中批评者不是说 metaphilosophy 不够激进，而是担心它太反思会拖慢进展。

B. 第三段直接说 critics worry this reflexivity may stall progress，这正对应“可能妨碍哲学实现其使命/推进工作”。

C. 文章没有说它被用来压制新思想，这个说法超出了原文。

D. 文中没有说它 incapable of evaluating diverse traditions，反而是在强调要更谨慎地跨文化比较。
reading.translation:
以下哪项是文中提到的对元哲学的一项批评？

元哲学批判性地探讨哲学探究能否真正超越文化与语言边界。传统哲学常追求普遍真理，元哲学则质疑此类真理在不同语境中是否可达。语言远非中立容器，它塑造并限制观念的表达与理解。在某一文化中深具共鸣的概念，在另一文化中可能含义全异，甚至不存在。这令人怀疑在特定文化土壤中形成的哲学框架能否全球适用：我们是在揭示真理，还是在强化文化偶然的假定？
有人主张，尽管语言与文化各异，苦难、正义、死亡等哲学关切跨社会共享，为普遍性提供基础。但即便这些主题也可能经文化特定透镜被解读。元哲学并不否定跨文化对话，但提醒勿假定其畅通无阻，并鼓励哲学家审视自身方法与假定如何跨语境旅行，或为何失败。
批评者担心这种反思会阻滞进展，也有人视其为避免智识越界的必要。通过凸显这些张力，元哲学并非稀释哲学目标，而是以更强自我意识与方法严谨性使其更锐利。

listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an architecture class.

Man: Have you ever thought about how ancient concrete structures like Roman amphitheaters and aqueducts have managed to last for thousands of years, while modern concrete buildings seem to fall apart and need replacing after just a few decades? For a long time, researchers thought the secret to Roman concrete's durability was volcanic ash. That makes sense, since volcanic ash was a major ingredient, and it was described as such by architects and historians who were writing at the time. But it turns out the real secret was actually tiny chunks of calcium carbonate. These formed because the Romans used dry quicklime in their mix, instead of the way we make concrete today, called Portland cement, where lime gets mixed with water first and then blended with everything else. When cracks show up in Roman concrete and water enters, those calcium carbonate bits react with the water and seal up the cracks. So the concrete basically heals itself, fixes the cracks, and gets stronger over time. The funny thing is, researchers have noticed these chunks in Roman concrete for ages, but they just figured they were a production flaw, like someone didn't mix the ingredients well enough. Anyway, considering how short-lived modern concrete is, and the fact that making it is bad for the environment, it's pretty exciting to think we might use some of these ancient Roman tricks in future construction.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段建筑学课的讲座。

男：你是否想过，罗马圆形剧场与高架渠等古代混凝土结构如何能存续数千年，而现代混凝土建筑似乎几十年就开裂、需要更换？长期来研究者以为罗马混凝土耐久的秘密是火山灰。这说得通，因为火山灰是主要成分，当时建筑师与历史学家也如此描述。但事实证明真正秘密其实是碳酸钙小块。它们形成是因为罗马人在混合料中使用干生石灰，而不是我们今天做混凝土的方式——波特兰水泥，即先把石灰与水混合再与其他成分拌合。当罗马混凝土出现裂缝、水进入时，那些碳酸钙颗粒与水反应并封闭裂缝。于是混凝土基本上自我愈合、修复裂缝，并随时间变强。有趣的是，研究者很久就注意到罗马混凝土中的这些小块，却以为只是生产瑕疵，像有人没把配料拌匀。无论如何，考虑到现代混凝土寿命短，以及生产对环境有害，想到我们或许在未来建筑中使用这些古罗马技巧，相当令人兴奋。

When cracks show up in Roman concrete and water enters, those calcium carbonate bits react with the water and seal up the cracks. So the concrete basically heals itself, fixes the cracks, and gets stronger over time. The funny thing is, researchers have noticed these chunks in Roman concrete for ages, but they just figured they were a production flaw, like someone didn't mix the ingredients well enough. Anyway, considering how short-lived modern concrete is, and the fact that making it is bad for the environment, it's pretty exciting to think we might use some of these ancient Roman tricks in future construction.

listening.translation: 讲座的主要话题是什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology class.

Human activities produce large amounts of organic waste like fruit scraps, yard waste and paper products. This waste can build up as trash. We can put it in landfills, but there it decomposes anaerobically — meaning without oxygen. Anaerobic decomposition results in the release of methane, a gas that significantly contributes to undesirable global warming.

But we have an alternative to landfills: composting. In composting, organic waste is broken down in special conditions by microorganisms, fungi, and sometimes insects. These organisms break down organic material into a dark, crumbly, earthy-smelling substance called humus. Unlike decomposition in landfills, composting occurs aerobically — or with oxygen — and therefore doesn't produce methane gas.

To compost effectively, you need the right balance of four things. One is nitrogen-rich materials, also known as greens — things like fruit and vegetable scraps. The second one is carbon-rich materials, or browns, like dry leaves, wood chips and paper waste. And you also need water and air, so the process does require proper management.

Humus, the primary product of composting, is full of essential nutrients. Adding it to soil enhances plant growth and increases agricultural yields. This reduces the need for chemical fertilizers. Humus-enriched soil also provides a habitat for microorganisms, insects and worms that in turn help decompose organic material and maintain soil health. This creates a virtuous circle of sorts.

In contrast, while chemical fertilizers can boost agricultural productivity in the short term, they are harmful to these beneficial organisms. They can actually damage the soil in the long run by killing the helpful organisms living in it.

请听一段生物学课的讲座。

人类活动产生大量有机废物，如果皮、庭院废弃物与纸制品。这些废物可堆积成垃圾。我们可以放进填埋场，但在那里它厌氧分解——意思是无氧。厌氧分解释放甲烷，这种气体显著助长不良的全球变暖。

但我们有填埋场的替代：堆肥。堆肥中，有机废物在特殊条件下由微生物、真菌，有时还有昆虫分解。这些生物把有机物分解成深色、易碎、有泥土气味的物质，称为腐殖质。与填埋场分解不同，堆肥在有氧条件下发生——因此不产生甲烷。

要有效堆肥，需要四样东西的正确平衡。一是富氮材料，也称绿色物——如蔬果边角料。二是富碳材料，或称棕色物，如干叶、木屑与纸废。还需要水与空气，因此过程确实需要妥善管理。

腐殖质——堆肥的主要产物——充满必需养分。加入土壤可增强植物生长、提高农业产量。这减少对化肥的需要。富含腐殖质的土壤也为微生物、昆虫与蠕虫提供栖息地，它们反过来帮助分解有机物并维持土壤健康。这形成某种良性循环。

相比之下，化肥虽可短期提高农业生产力，却对这些有益生物有害。长远看，它们实际上会通过杀死土中有益生物而损害土壤。

listening.translation: 演讲者主要讨论了什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology class.

Man: You've probably heard that ants can carry 50 times their own body weight. Amazing, right? Ants also have, on the front of their heads, strong mandibles. Mandibles are like jaws, though ants use them like pincers or grippers, similar to how humans use our thumb and index finger to pick things up. Now, ants' mandibles, their inner surfaces, are covered in tiny hairs. And researchers working on biomimicry, which means imitating nature in human inventions, recently wondered if they could use this idea in a robot gripper. A robot gripper is a device with flat plates that come together to pick things up. But it's difficult to pick up packaging with curved edges, so manufacturers often use grippers with three plates for stability. Three plates are bulky and harder to operate, making them awkward. So, the researchers built a robot gripper with two plates, adding tiny artificial hairs and copying ants' mandibles, and another gripper with just two smooth plates. They conducted over 2,000 tests, an astonishing number, I think, comparing how well the grippers picked up items like a cereal box and a shampoo bottle. The hairy gripper was at least 29 percent better at grabbing and holding onto items. Its grip was more gentle and more secure.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段生物学课的讲座。

男：你大概听说过蚂蚁能搬动自身体重五十倍的东西。神奇，对吧？蚂蚁头部前方还有强壮的大颚。大颚像颌，不过蚂蚁像钳子或夹具那样用它们，类似人类用拇指与食指抓东西。蚂蚁大颚的内表面覆盖着细毛。从事仿生学——意思是在人类发明中模仿自然——的研究者最近想知道能否把这一想法用于机器人夹爪。机器人夹爪是用平板合拢抓取物体的装置。但抓取带曲面边缘的包装很难，所以制造商常为稳定性使用三板夹爪。三板笨重、更难操作，显得别扭。于是研究者做了带两板并加微小人造毛、模仿蚂蚁大颚的机器人夹爪，以及只有两块光滑板的另一夹爪。他们做了超过两千次测试——我认为数量惊人——比较夹爪抓取麦片盒与洗发水瓶等物品的表现。带毛夹爪在抓取与持物上至少好百分之二十九。其抓握更轻柔也更稳固。

男：你大概听说过蚂蚁能搬动自身体重五十倍的东西。神奇，对吧？蚂蚁头部前方还有强壮的大颚。大颚像颌，不过蚂蚁像钳子或夹具那样用它们，类似人类用拇指与食指抓东西。蚂蚁大颚的内表面覆盖着细毛。从事仿生学——意思是在人类发明中模仿自然——的研究者最近想知道能否把这一想法用于机器人夹爪。机器人夹爪是用平板合拢抓取物体的装置。但抓取带曲面边缘的包装很难，所以制造商常为稳定性使用三板夹爪。三板笨重、更难操作，显得别扭。于是研究者做了带两板并加微小人造毛、模仿蚂蚁大颚的机器人夹爪，以及只有两块光滑板的另一夹爪。他们做了超过两千次测试——我认为数量惊人——比较夹爪抓取麦片盒与洗发水瓶等物品的表现。带毛夹爪在抓取与持物上至少好百分之二十九。其抓握更轻柔也更稳固。

listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology class.

Man: You've probably heard that ants can carry 50 times their own body weight. Amazing, right? Ants also have, on the front of their heads, strong mandibles. Mandibles are like jaws, though ants use them like pincers or grippers, similar to how humans use our thumb and index finger to pick things up. Now, ants' mandibles, their inner surfaces, are covered in tiny hairs. And researchers working on biomimicry, which means imitating nature in human inventions, recently wondered if they could use this idea in a robot gripper. A robot gripper is a device with flat plates that come together to pick things up. But it's difficult to pick up packaging with curved edges, so manufacturers often use grippers with three plates for stability. Three plates are bulky and harder to operate, making them awkward. So, the researchers built a robot gripper with two plates, adding tiny artificial hairs and copying ants' mandibles, and another gripper with just two smooth plates. They conducted over 2,000 tests, an astonishing number, I think, comparing how well the grippers picked up items like a cereal box and a shampoo bottle. The hairy gripper was at least 29 percent better at grabbing and holding onto items. Its grip was more gentle and more secure.

listening.translation: 讲座的主要话题是什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a history class.

Man: Before we say any more about textiles, let's talk about the historical indigo trade. Indigo is a natural blue dye that comes from the leaves of Indigofera plants. Today, you see it most often in blue jeans. Indigo was a staple export for hundreds of years. There was a time when only rice was more valuable. The English began importing it during the early 1600s from India, and British colonists started growing it in North America about a century later. Natural indigo nearly vanished from industrial use by the early 20th century after German chemists invented a synthetic alternative. This was cheaper and more efficient for large-scale production. For decades, natural indigo survived only in niche applications and local traditions. Today, indigo is back as a viable commercial crop in places like Bangladesh and the United States. This is partly thanks to the fashion industry's efforts to be more environmentally sustainable, and many now see natural indigo as a symbol of ethical consumption. Its value as a commodity also lies in its versatility. It is also used in cosmetics and food coloring. Farmers find it to be low maintenance with high returns. One hectare can yield thousands of kilograms of leaves. The economic incentive is clear: minimal input, high output, and growing international interest. That said, the traditional fermentation techniques for extracting the dye are extremely labor-intensive, which makes natural indigo expensive. And some producers claiming natural methods still rely on harsh chemicals, which undermines the dye's eco-friendly reputation.

speaking.answer: Right now I'm a full-time student, but I've had a couple of different part-time jobs. The most recent one was at a small bookstore near my university, where I worked about fifteen hours a week. Um, I helped customers find books, ran the cash register, and organized new arrivals on the shelves. Before that, in high school, I worked one summer at my uncle's restaurant as a waiter. Honestly, both jobs taught me different things. The restaurant was fast and noisy, so I learned to stay calm under pressure. speaking.answer: At the bookstore, my duties changed a bit from day to day, but a few tasks were regular. speaking.answer: One challenging project was a group presentation in my business class. content.promptText: Good. Some people believe that gaining diverse work experiences by often changing jobs and companies is more valuable than staying in one job or one company for a long time. What is your opinion on this? Why?

speaking.answer: Hmm, I see both sides, but I lean toward staying longer. When you change jobs often, you do see different workplaces and meet more people, and that can be exciting. But I think you only learn the deep skills when you stay and face the hard problems. My aunt worked at the same company for ten years, and she grew from an assistant to a manager because everyone trusted her. On the other hand, a few moves early in a career can help you figure out what you like. So I'd say a balance works best. Try a couple of different jobs when you're young and still exploring, then settle somewhere you can really grow, and, you know, build something lasting.

writing.answer: In my opinion, cultural globalization brings both loss and enrichment, but with care its benefits can outweigh its costs. I agree with Kelly that as global culture spreads, unique traditions and languages risk being forgotten or replaced, which is a real danger to diversity that communities should actively guard against. Once a language disappears, much knowledge is lost with it. However, Andrew makes a strong point that globalization also promotes exchange and understanding, letting people appreciate other cultures and creating a more tolerant, interconnected world. Therefore, I believe the goal should be balance: communities can embrace useful global ideas while consciously preserving and celebrating their own traditions through education, festivals, and local media. In this way, cultural globalization does not have to erase local identity; instead, it can encourage cultures to interact and learn from one another while keeping what makes each of them distinctive and meaningful.

content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: Grasshoppers are insects commonly found in dry places with grass and plants. Grasshoppers [1] ha__ several [2] wa__ they [3] pro____ themselves [4] aga____ danger. [5] Th__ have [6] powe____ back [7] le__, which [8] al___ them [9] t_ jump [10] aw__ from enemies, such as rodents and snakes. Some grasshoppers can jump twenty times the length of their bodies. By the time they are adults, grasshoppers can also fly. Adult grasshoppers fly very quickly and this helps them avoid danger.

reading.answer:
1. ve → have
2. ys → ways
3. tect → protect
4. inst → against
5. ey → They
6. rful → powerful
7. gs → legs
8. low → allow
9. o → to
10. ay → away
reading.explanation: 1. have 表示'有'，是句子的谓语动词，与主语 Grasshoppers 配合，描述蚱蜢拥有几种保护自己的方式。 2. ways 意思是'方式'，several ways 表示几种方式，在句子中作宾语，指蚱蜢保护自己的方法。 3. protect 表示'保护'，themselves 是反身代词，protect themselves 意思是蚱蜢保护自己免受危险。 4. against 表示'对抗'，与 danger 搭配，意思是抵御危险，说明保护的目标。 5. They 指代前文的 Grasshoppers，在句子中作主语，引出蚱蜢拥有的后腿特征。 6. powerful 表示'强大的'，形容 back legs 的特性，强调后腿的力量。 7. legs 意思是'腿'，back legs 特指后腿，是蚱蜢跳跃的身体部位。 8. allow 表示'允许'，allow sb to do sth. 是固定结构，意思是后腿使蚱蜢能够跳跃逃离敌人。 9. to 是不定式符号，与 jump 构成不定式，表示目的或动作，连接 allow 和 jump。 10. away 表示'离开'，jump away 意思是跳开，描述蚱蜢从敌人身边逃离的动作。
reading.translation: 蝗虫是常见于有草与植物的干燥地方的昆虫。蝗虫有多种保护自己免受危险的方式。它们有有力的后腿，可跳离啮齿动物与蛇等敌人。一些蝗虫可跳到身体长度二十倍远。成年后，蝗虫也能飞。成年蝗虫飞得很快，这帮助它们躲避危险。

reading.title: Pigments and Paint Mixing
reading.prompt: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.

It [1] w__ once [2] com___ for [3] art____ to [4] cre___ their [5] o__ paints [6] b_ mixing [7] sev____ pigments [8] toge____. This [9] pro____ was [10] ti__-consuming and required detailed knowledge of pigments—their chemical properties, how they interact with different media, and their durability over time. But it also allowed painters to give their artworks a truly unique color palette.

content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: Pigments are substances that provide color to materials, and they can be derived from various natural sources, such as minerals and plants. It [1] w__ once [2] com___ for [3] art____ to [4] cre___ their [5] o__ paints [6] b_ mixing [7] sev____ pigments [8] toge____. This [9] pro____ was [10] ti__-consuming and required detailed knowledge of pigments—their chemical properties, how they interact with different media, and their durability over time. But it also allowed painters to give their artworks a truly unique color palette.

reading.answer:
1. as → was
2. mon → common
3. ists → artists
4. ate → create
5. wn → own
6. y → by
7. eral → several
8. ther → together
9. cess → process
10. me → time
reading.explanation: 1. It 作为形式主语，后接谓语动词描述过去状态，因此填 was。 2. 形容词 common 修饰不定式短语，表示这种行为很常见。 3. 名词 artists 作 for 的宾语，指代进行创作的艺术家们。 4. 动词 create 是不定式原形，表示创建颜料的动作。 5. 形容词 own 强调颜料是艺术家自己制作的。 6. 介词 by 引出方式状语，说明创建颜料的方法。 7. 形容词 several 表示数量，指混合多种颜料。 8. 副词 together 修饰 mixing，表示将颜料混合到一起。 9. 名词 process 指代前文提到的创建颜料的过程。 10. 名词 time 与 consuming 构成复合形容词，表示耗时。
reading.translation: 颜料是为材料提供颜色的物质，可来自矿物与植物等多种自然来源。曾几何时，艺术家常通过混合多种颜料自制颜料。这一过程耗时，并需要关于颜料的详细知识——其化学性质、如何与不同介质相互作用，以及随时间的耐久性。但它也使画家能为作品赋予真正独特的色板。

reading.prompt: The word "anomalies" in the passage is closest in meaning to
reading.promptZh: 文中“anomalies”一词最接近下列哪个词的含义？
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1

Paragraph 1
Ecological Systems Theory, introduced by Urie Bronfenbrenner, revolutionized our perception of human psychological development. 【位置 1】 It posits that individuals are shaped by interactions among multiple overlapping environmental systems. 【位置 2】 This theory reshaped developmental research, offering a multi-faceted lens that surpasses earlier, linear models. 【位置 3】 By considering the dynamic interplay between a person and their environment, it highlights the multifactorial nature of psychological growth. 【位置 4】

The theory delineates several environmental layers, beginning with the microsystem, which refers to the institutions and groups that most directly impact the child's development, such as family and school. reading.translation:
作者在第2段提及“老师与家长的沟通”的目的是什么？

尤里·布朗芬布伦纳提出的生态系统理论彻底改变了我们对人类心理发展的理解。它主张个体由多个相互重叠的环境系统之间的互动所塑造。该理论重塑了发展研究，提供了超越早期线性模型的多面向视角。通过考虑人与环境的动态互动，它凸显了心理成长的多因素本质。
理论划分多层环境：最内层是微系统，指最直接影响儿童发展的机构与群体，如家庭与学校。中系统涵盖微系统之间的关系，例如教师与家长的沟通如何影响孩子的教育。其外是外系统，由父母职场压力等间接影响构成，会微妙作用于家庭环境。宏系统则涵盖更广的文化与社会语境，以底层规范与政策框定这些互动。
尽管布朗芬布伦纳模型框架精巧，仍有批评。有人认为它低估了技术作用——技术已创造出超越地理限制的虚拟微系统。即便如此，该理论在教育到公共政策等诸多领域仍具影响，并持续推动对其应用与调适的探索。

Ecological Systems Theory, introduced by Urie Bronfenbrenner, revolutionized our perception of human psychological development. 【位置 1】 It posits that individuals are shaped by interactions among multiple overlapping environmental systems. 【位置 2】 This theory reshaped developmental research, offering a multi-faceted lens that surpasses earlier, linear models. 【位置 3】 By considering the dynamic interplay between a person and their environment, it highlights the multifactorial nature of psychological growth. 【位置 4】

Paragraph 2
The theory delineates several environmental layers, beginning with the microsystem, which refers to the institutions and groups that most directly impact the child's development, such as family and school. The mesosystem encompasses the relationships among the microsystems, such as the impact of a teacher's communication with parents on a child's education. Beyond these, the exosystem consists of indirect influences like a parent's workplace stress subtly affecting the home environment. The macrosystem, encompassing broader cultural and societal contexts, frames these interactions with underlying norms and policies.

Paragraph 3
While Bronfenbrenner's model offers an intricate framework, it is not without critique. Some argue that the model underestimates the role of technology, which has created virtual microsystems that transcend geographical limits. Despite these critiques, the theory remains influential in fields ranging from education to public policy, prompting continuous exploration of its applications and adaptations.

reading.translation:
文中有四个位置可以添加以下句子：“每个系统在塑造行为方面都发挥着独特的作用。”这个句子最适合放在哪里？

尤里·布朗芬布伦纳提出的生态系统理论彻底改变了我们对人类心理发展的理解。它主张个体由多个相互重叠的环境系统之间的互动所塑造。该理论重塑了发展研究，提供了超越早期线性模型的多面向视角。通过考虑人与环境的动态互动，它凸显了心理成长的多因素本质。
理论划分多层环境：最内层是微系统，指最直接影响儿童发展的机构与群体，如家庭与学校。中系统涵盖微系统之间的关系，例如教师与家长的沟通如何影响孩子的教育。其外是外系统，由父母职场压力等间接影响构成，会微妙作用于家庭环境。宏系统则涵盖更广的文化与社会语境，以底层规范与政策框定这些互动。
尽管布朗芬布伦纳模型框架精巧，仍有批评。有人认为它低估了技术作用——技术已创造出超越地理限制的虚拟微系统。即便如此，该理论在教育到公共政策等诸多领域仍具影响，并持续推动对其应用与调适的探索。

'sustaining li__'中需要名词'life'，表示维持生命。 5. 'for____ the found_____'中需要动词，前缀'for'对应'forming'，表示形成基础。 6. 'found_____'指食物链的基础，单词'foundation'意为'基础'。 7. 'f___ chains'指食物链，前缀'f'对应单词'food'，意为'食物'。 8. reading.translation: 光合作用对地球生命至关重要，也有潜力应对现代能源挑战。通过把阳光转化为化学能，植物产生氧气与有机化合物，维持生命并构成食物链基础。人工光合作用理论上可提供清洁可再生的能源，减少对化石燃料的依赖。通过模拟光合作用，科学家可生产碳中性燃料，有助于发展可持续能源方案。

reading.title: Electromagnetic Healing
reading.prompt: The word "promoting" in the passage is closest in meaning to
reading.promptZh: 文中单词“promoting”最接近的意思是
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Advances in traumatology have highlighted the potential of electromagnetic fields (EMFs) in promoting bone healing. EMFs, invisible areas of energy produced by electrically charged objects, are recognized for their therapeutic benefits. Researchers have found that specific EMF frequencies can stimulate cellular activity, enhancing bone repair. Unlike traditional treatments such as metal implants and bone grafts, EMF therapy is non-invasive and produces few side effects. In clinical studies, patients with non-healing fractures exposed to EMFs showed significant improvement. One study showed that EMFs reduced recovery time by accelerating healing by up to 50 percent, a significant difference for patients with conditions that impede natural healing.

Paragraph 2
Multiple mechanisms driven by EMFs have been identified as contributing to bone healing, yet the complete picture is not fully understood. Some scientists believe that EMFs enhance the production of substances known as growth factors, which include essential proteins for cell growth and repair. Others note that EMFs improve blood circulation to the damaged area, facilitating nutrient delivery and waste removal. Researchers are uncertain of how the mechanisms interact, the optimal parameters (frequency, intensity, duration) for therapies, and the relation between the amount of a treatment and the magnitude of the effect it produces. 【位置 4】

reading.translation:
文中单词“promoting”最接近的意思是

创伤学进展凸显了电磁场（EMF）促进骨愈合的潜力。EMF 是带电物体产生的不可见能量区域，其治疗益处已获认识。研究发现特定频率可刺激细胞活动、增强骨修复。与金属植入、植骨等传统疗法不同，EMF 治疗无创且副作用少。临床研究中，不愈合骨折患者接受 EMF 后显著改善；一项研究显示其可加速愈合、最多缩短约一半恢复时间，对自然愈合受阻的患者意义重大。
已识别多种由 EMF 驱动、有助于骨愈合的机制，但全貌仍未完全明了。有科学家认为 EMF 促进生长因子（包括细胞生长与修复所需蛋白）的产生；也有人指出 EMF 改善损伤区血液循环，便于营养输送与废物清除。这些机制如何相互作用、疗法的最优参数（频率、强度、时长），以及剂量与效应大小的关系，研究者仍不确定。

reading.translation:
文章提到以下哪项是关于促成骨愈合的电磁场驱动机制尚不明确的？

创伤学进展凸显了电磁场（EMF）促进骨愈合的潜力。EMF 是带电物体产生的不可见能量区域，其治疗益处已获认识。研究发现特定频率可刺激细胞活动、增强骨修复。与金属植入、植骨等传统疗法不同，EMF 治疗无创且副作用少。临床研究中，不愈合骨折患者接受 EMF 后显著改善；一项研究显示其可加速愈合、最多缩短约一半恢复时间，对自然愈合受阻的患者意义重大。
已识别多种由 EMF 驱动、有助于骨愈合的机制，但全貌仍未完全明了。有科学家认为 EMF 促进生长因子（包括细胞生长与修复所需蛋白）的产生；也有人指出 EMF 改善损伤区血液循环，便于营养输送与废物清除。这些机制如何相互作用、疗法的最优参数（频率、强度、时长），以及剂量与效应大小的关系，研究者仍不确定。

reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Advances in traumatology have highlighted the potential of electromagnetic fields (EMFs) in promoting bone healing. EMFs, invisible areas of energy produced by electrically charged objects, are recognized for their therapeutic benefits. Researchers have found that specific EMF frequencies can stimulate cellular activity, enhancing bone repair. Unlike traditional treatments such as metal implants and bone grafts, EMF therapy is non-invasive and produces few side effects. In clinical studies, patients with non-healing fractures exposed to EMFs showed significant improvement. One study showed that EMFs reduced recovery time by accelerating healing by up to 50 percent, a significant difference for patients with conditions that impede natural healing.

Paragraph 2
【位置 1】 Multiple mechanisms driven by EMFs have been identified as contributing to bone healing, yet the complete picture is not fully understood. 【位置 2】 Some scientists believe that EMFs enhance the production of substances known as growth factors, which include essential proteins for cell growth and repair. 【位置 3】 Others note that EMFs improve blood circulation to the damaged area, facilitating nutrient delivery and waste removal. Researchers are uncertain of how the mechanisms interact, the optimal parameters (frequency, intensity, duration) for therapies, and the relation between the amount of a treatment and the magnitude of the effect it produces. 【位置 4】

listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a music class.

Man: Have you ever listened to a piece of music and suddenly felt like you were somewhere else? Maybe walking through a Brazilian street market or climbing a misty mountain trail in China? That's the magic of musical borrowing, a practice where artists blend elements from different global traditions to create something fresh and emotionally resonant. Take bossa nova, for example. It's a genre that merges the laid-back swing of United States jazz music with the rhythmic pulse of Brazilian samba. When you listen to bossa nova, it feels both familiar and new at the same time. But successful musical borrowing isn't just about mixing sounds. It's about respect. When artists draw from other cultures, they need to understand the traditions behind the music. Composer Tan Dun nails this in his score for the film Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon. He blends Chinese instruments like the erhu and pipa with Western orchestration, but not just for effect. The erhu's haunting tones and the pipa's intricate rhythms reflect centuries of Chinese musical storytelling. Tan Dun doesn't just borrow; he honors the culture, letting its emotional depth shine through. Of course, fusion isn't always seamless. Sometimes the mix feels forced or the original meaning gets lost. But when it works, when the traditions truly speak to each other, it's proof that music can be a universal language, capable of bridging worlds and telling stories that transcend borders.

请听一段音乐课的讲座。

男：你是否曾听一段音乐突然感觉自己身在别处？也许走在巴西街市，或攀爬中国雾蒙蒙的山径？那是音乐借用的魔力——艺术家融合不同全球传统的元素，创造出新鲜且情感共鸣的东西。以波萨诺瓦为例。这一类型把美国爵士的慵懒摇摆与巴西桑巴的节奏脉动融合。听波萨诺瓦时，既熟悉又新颖。但成功的音乐借用不只是混音。它关乎尊重。当艺术家从其他文化汲取时，需要理解音乐背后的传统。作曲家谭盾在电影《卧虎藏龙》配乐中做到了这一点。他将二胡、琵琶等中国乐器与西方管弦乐融合，但不只为效果。二胡萦绕的音色与琵琶复杂的节奏反映数世纪中国音乐叙事。谭盾不只借用；他尊重文化，让其情感深度透出。当然，融合并非总是无缝。有时混合显得生硬，或原意丢失。但当它奏效、当传统真正彼此对话时，证明音乐可以是通用语言，能够连接世界、讲述跨越边界的故事。

男：你是否曾听一段音乐突然感觉自己身在别处？也许走在巴西街市，或攀爬中国雾蒙蒙的山径？那是音乐借用的魔力——艺术家融合不同全球传统的元素，创造出新鲜且情感共鸣的东西。以波萨诺瓦为例。这一类型把美国爵士的慵懒摇摆与巴西桑巴的节奏脉动融合。听波萨诺瓦时，既熟悉又新颖。但成功的音乐借用不只是混音。它关乎尊重。当艺术家从其他文化汲取时，需要理解音乐背后的传统。作曲家谭盾在电影《卧虎藏龙》配乐中做到了这一点。他将二胡、琵琶等中国乐器与西方管弦乐融合，但不只为效果。二胡萦绕的音色与琵琶复杂的节奏反映数世纪中国音乐叙事。谭盾不只借用；他尊重文化，让其情感深度透出。当然，融合并非总是无缝。有时混合显得生硬，或原意丢失。但当它奏效、当传统真正彼此对话时，证明音乐可以是通用语言，能够连接世界、讲述跨越边界的故事。

choices.reviewExplanationZh: 不选。提到电影 Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon，但没有说受小说启发。

choices.label: It shows a deep understanding of Chinese culture.
choices.labelZh: 它展现了对中国文化的深刻理解
choices.reviewExplanationZh: 正确。原文说 Tan Dun 不只是 borrow，而是 honors the culture，让 Chinese musical storytelling 的深度体现出来。

listening.answer: D. It shows a deep understanding of Chinese culture.

A. 不选。原文说体现 Chinese musical storytelling 的 emotional depth，不是 Tan Dun 自己的个人经历。

B. 不选。没有比较受众。

C. 不选。提到电影 Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon，但没有说受小说启发。

listening.translation: 关于谭盾的音乐，演讲者强调了什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a music class.

Man: Have you ever listened to a piece of music and suddenly felt like you were somewhere else? Maybe walking through a Brazilian street market or climbing a misty mountain trail in China? That's the magic of musical borrowing, a practice where artists blend elements from different global traditions to create something fresh and emotionally resonant. Take bossa nova, for example. It's a genre that merges the laid-back swing of United States jazz music with the rhythmic pulse of Brazilian samba. When you listen to bossa nova, it feels both familiar and new at the same time. But successful musical borrowing isn't just about mixing sounds. It's about respect. When artists draw from other cultures, they need to understand the traditions behind the music. Composer Tan Dun nails this in his score for the film Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon. He blends Chinese instruments like the erhu and pipa with Western orchestration, but not just for effect. The erhu's haunting tones and the pipa's intricate rhythms reflect centuries of Chinese musical storytelling. Tan Dun doesn't just borrow; he honors the culture, letting its emotional depth shine through. Of course, fusion isn't always seamless. Sometimes the mix feels forced or the original meaning gets lost. But when it works, when the traditions truly speak to each other, it's proof that music can be a universal language, capable of bridging worlds and telling stories that transcend borders.

listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a business class.

Woman: Today we're discussing the concept of dark stores, which are retail centers that resemble warehouses and are usually located near city centers. Unlike traditional storefronts, they are not designed for walk-in customers, but function as fulfillment hubs optimized for rapid online delivery. The rise of dark stores has been fueled by the growing demand for online shopping, especially in urban areas where space is limited and rent is high. The main appeal of dark stores lies in their efficiency. By eliminating the traditional storefront, businesses can reduce overhead and pass savings on to consumers through lower prices. Their proximity to dense urban areas also allows for faster delivery times, meeting the expectations of customers who value speed and convenience. For instance, a company might deliver groceries in under an hour, giving it a major competitive advantage over traditional supermarkets. However, dark stores are not without drawbacks. Their expansion can contribute to the decline of traditional retail spaces, creating economic challenges for local businesses. Employment is another concern. While these centers generate jobs in logistics and delivery, they may reduce the number of customer-facing roles available in physical stores. Looking ahead, many experts predict that dark stores will continue to reshape the retail landscape. Some may adopt advanced automation, further reducing the need for human labor and potentially redefining the shopping experience itself. As with other technological shifts, the key challenge will be balancing efficiency with the broader social and economic implications of these changes.

listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a business class.

Woman: Today we're discussing the concept of dark stores, which are retail centers that resemble warehouses and are usually located near city centers. Unlike traditional storefronts, they are not designed for walk-in customers, but function as fulfillment hubs optimized for rapid online delivery. The rise of dark stores has been fueled by the growing demand for online shopping, especially in urban areas where space is limited and rent is high. The main appeal of dark stores lies in their efficiency. By eliminating the traditional storefront, businesses can reduce overhead and pass savings on to consumers through lower prices. Their proximity to dense urban areas also allows for faster delivery times, meeting the expectations of customers who value speed and convenience. For instance, a company might deliver groceries in under an hour, giving it a major competitive advantage over traditional supermarkets. However, dark stores are not without drawbacks. Their expansion can contribute to the decline of traditional retail spaces, creating economic challenges for local businesses. Employment is another concern. While these centers generate jobs in logistics and delivery, they may reduce the number of customer-facing roles available in physical stores. Looking ahead, many experts predict that dark stores will continue to reshape the retail landscape. Some may adopt advanced automation, further reducing the need for human labor and potentially redefining the shopping experience itself. As with other technological shifts, the key challenge will be balancing efficiency with the broader social and economic implications of these changes.

listening.translation: 讲座的主要话题是什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology class.

Man: Frogs aren't just known for their croaks and leaps; they're key players in ecosystems, acting as both predators and prey. But scientists have been sounding the alarm: frog populations are shrinking fast across the globe. One major reason is chemical pollution. Pesticides and other pollutants often end up in the water where frogs live and breed. These chemicals interfere with their reproductive systems, leading to fewer eggs and developmental issues in tadpoles. Over time, this can cause entire populations to collapse. Another serious threat is disease, especially a fungus called chytrid. This fungus attacks the skin of frogs, which is vital for absorbing water and regulating electrolytes. Infected frogs often become lethargic, lose coordination, and eventually die. Chytrid has spread rapidly and is responsible for declines and extinctions in hundreds of frog species worldwide. It's one of the most devastating wildlife diseases ever recorded. Why is this problematic? Frogs also serve as indicators of environmental health because they're so sensitive to changes in water quality and temperature. Their decline often signals deeper ecological problems. Bees play a similar role. When bee populations drop, it can point to issues like pesticide overuse or habitat stress. When frogs and bees are struggling, it's a warning sign that the environment needs attention.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段生物学课的讲座。

listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a physics class.

Man: Today we're going to explore a phenomenon called thin film interference. This is an optical effect that occurs when light interacts with very thin surfaces. Imagine a soap bubble floating in the air. Although it's made of clear liquid, it shines with shifting rainbow colors. Thin film interference explains how this shimmering display occurs when light strikes a bubble. Some light reflects off the outer surface, and some reflects off the inner surface. As these waves meet, they can either reinforce one another or cancel each other out. If the waves reinforce one another, the color looks brighter. This is called constructive interference because the waves are building the light. If the waves cancel each other out, the color fades. This is called destructive interference because the waves are negating each other's effect. Which color appears depends on factors that constantly change, such as the thickness of the film and the angle of the incoming light. As these factors shift, some wavelengths are reinforced while others are canceled, producing the bubble's rainbow shimmer. The thin film that creates these dazzling colors also makes the bubble fragile, because the layer is so delicate. The bubble can burst with the slightest touch or breeze. Scientists are interested in applying thin-film interference to technology. Possible uses include paints that shine with bright colors without pigments, and anti-reflective coatings for lenses. However, achieving a reproducible natural balance of simplicity and efficiency remains a significant challenge.

男：今天我们探索一种叫薄膜干涉的现象。这是光与极薄表面相互作用时发生的光学效应。想象空中漂浮的肥皂泡。虽然由透明液体构成，它却闪耀着变幻的彩虹色。薄膜干涉解释了光打在泡上时这种闪烁如何发生。一些光从外表面反射，一些从内表面反射。这些波相遇时，要么相互加强，要么相互抵消。若波相互加强，颜色显得更亮。这叫相长干涉，因为波在叠加光。若波相互抵消，颜色变淡。这叫相消干涉，因为波在抵消彼此的效果。出现哪种颜色取决于不断变化的因素，如薄膜厚度与入射光角度。这些因素变化时，某些波长被加强而另一些被抵消，产生泡的彩虹闪烁。制造这些炫目色彩的薄膜也使泡脆弱，因为那一层极细。最轻微的触碰或微风就能使泡破裂。科学家有兴趣把薄膜干涉应用于技术。可能用途包括无需颜料即可闪耀亮色的涂料，以及镜头的抗反射涂层。然而，实现可复现的自然简洁与效率平衡仍是重大挑战。

listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a physics class.

Man: Today we're going to explore a phenomenon called thin film interference. This is an optical effect that occurs when light interacts with very thin surfaces. Imagine a soap bubble floating in the air. Although it's made of clear liquid, it shines with shifting rainbow colors. Thin film interference explains how this shimmering display occurs when light strikes a bubble. Some light reflects off the outer surface, and some reflects off the inner surface. As these waves meet, they can either reinforce one another or cancel each other out. If the waves reinforce one another, the color looks brighter. This is called constructive interference because the waves are building the light. If the waves cancel each other out, the color fades. This is called destructive interference because the waves are negating each other's effect. Which color appears depends on factors that constantly change, such as the thickness of the film and the angle of the incoming light. As these factors shift, some wavelengths are reinforced while others are canceled, producing the bubble's rainbow shimmer. The thin film that creates these dazzling colors also makes the bubble fragile, because the layer is so delicate. The bubble can burst with the slightest touch or breeze. Scientists are interested in applying thin-film interference to technology. Possible uses include paints that shine with bright colors without pigments, and anti-reflective coatings for lenses. However, achieving a reproducible natural balance of simplicity and efficiency remains a significant challenge.

请听一段物理课的讲座。

男：今天我们探索一种叫薄膜干涉的现象。这是光与极薄表面相互作用时发生的光学效应。想象空中漂浮的肥皂泡。虽然由透明液体构成，它却闪耀着变幻的彩虹色。薄膜干涉解释了光打在泡上时这种闪烁如何发生。一些光从外表面反射，一些从内表面反射。这些波相遇时，要么相互加强，要么相互抵消。若波相互加强，颜色显得更亮。这叫相长干涉，因为波在叠加光。若波相互抵消，颜色变淡。这叫相消干涉，因为波在抵消彼此的效果。出现哪种颜色取决于不断变化的因素，如薄膜厚度与入射光角度。这些因素变化时，某些波长被加强而另一些被抵消，产生泡的彩虹闪烁。制造这些炫目色彩的薄膜也使泡脆弱，因为那一层极细。最轻微的触碰或微风就能使泡破裂。科学家有兴趣把薄膜干涉应用于技术。可能用途包括无需颜料即可闪耀亮色的涂料，以及镜头的抗反射涂层。然而，实现可复现的自然简洁与效率平衡仍是重大挑战。

content.promptText: Thank you for participating in the study. I'd like to ask you some questions about your job satisfaction. First, what do you think are the most important things to consider when looking for a job?

speaking.answer: For me, the most important thing is probably the people I'd work with. If my coworkers and manager are supportive, even a difficult job feels manageable. Salary matters too, of course, because I need to pay rent and, uh, save a little for the future. But I wouldn't take a high-paying job if it meant working endless hours and having no personal time. So work-life balance is another big one. And I'd also look for a place where I can learn new skills and grow, because I don't want to do the same thing for ten years. Honestly, if a job gives me decent pay, good people, and room to develop, I'd feel pretty satisfied with it. A short commute would be a nice bonus too. That's really what I'd look for.
speaking.translation: 感谢你参与这项研究。我想问你一些关于工作满意度的问题。首先，你认为在找工作时最重要的考量是什么？

content.promptText: Now, can you describe a job that either you or one of your friends has had? What kind of work was involved?

speaking.answer: Well, my friend Mia worked last summer as a waitress at a small seafood restaurant near the beach. Her day started around ten in the morning, when she helped set up the tables and learned the daily specials. Then, uh, when customers arrived, she took orders, brought out the food, and answered questions about the menu. She also had to deal with complaints sometimes, like when a dish took too long. On busy weekends she was on her feet for almost eight hours, and she came home exhausted. Her favorite job was folding the napkins before opening, because it was quiet and she could chat with the cooks. But she said she liked meeting new people, and the tips were pretty good. I think the job also taught her how to stay calm under pressure, which is useful in any career.

content.promptText: I see. What kinds of things do you think can lead people to feel unhappy in their work? Can you tell me about one or two of them?

speaking.answer: Hmm, I think there are a few things, but two stand out for me. The first is a bad relationship with a manager. If your boss criticizes everything and never says thank you, you start dreading Monday mornings. I've seen my cousin go through that, and it really wore him down. The second is feeling that your work has no meaning or no future. Like, if you do the same boring task every day and never get a chance to learn or move up, you just feel stuck. Low pay and long hours can make things worse, of course. But I mean, people can handle a lot when they feel respected and see a purpose, so those two are the big ones.

content.promptText: Last question. Some people believe that working for a large company offers more advantages than working for a small company, while others prefer the opposite. What do you think, and why?

speaking.answer: I'd say I lean toward small companies, although both have good points. A large company usually offers higher salaries, better benefits, and a famous name on your resume. That's attractive, especially for someone just starting out. But, um, I think small companies give you more chances to try different things. You might help with marketing one day and customer service the next, so you learn much faster. Plus, everyone knows each other, and your ideas can actually be heard instead of getting lost in many levels of management. I'd probably pick a small company at the start of my career for the experience. Later, if I wanted more stability, I could always move to a bigger one. So for me, the learning matters more than the name.
speaking.translation: 最后一个问题。有些人认为在大公司工作比在小公司工作优势更多，而另一些人则相反。你怎么看，为什么？

writing.answer:
Dear Ms. Lopez,

I am a regular customer at your bakery and have always loved your fresh bread and pastries, which is why I chose you for a special cake for my professor.

A customer

content.promptText: Your professor is teaching a class on economics. Write a post responding to the professor's question.
content.stimulusText: Your professor is teaching a class on economics. Write a post responding to the professor's question. Express and support your opinion. Make a contribution to the discussion in your own words. An effective response will contain at least 100 words. We often discuss the impact of government intervention in the economy. Some argue that government regulations and policies can improve economic stability and protect consumers. Others believe that too much intervention can stifle innovation and lead to inefficiencies. What do you think is the most effective role of government in the economy?
content.post: Andrew: In my opinion, too much government intervention can hinder economic growth and innovation. Businesses need the freedom to operate without excessive regulations, which can be costly and create inefficiencies. The economy would benefit more from government with a limited role.

writing.answer: In my opinion, the most effective role of government in the economy is a balanced one that regulates without over-controlling. I agree with Claire that government intervention is important for ensuring stability and protecting consumers, since well-designed rules can prevent harmful business practices, stop monopolies, and maintain fair competition. Without any oversight, markets can become unstable and exploit ordinary people. However, Andrew makes a valid point that excessive regulation can raise costs, slow decision-making, and stifle the innovation that drives growth. Therefore, I believe the government should focus on setting clear, essential rules, protecting consumers and workers, and stepping in during crises, while leaving enough freedom for businesses to compete and experiment. This middle path captures the strengths of both views: it keeps the economy fair and stable while still allowing the flexibility and risk-taking that long-term innovation and prosperity require.

reading.prompt: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
reading.passage: Learning the controlled use of fire was a key development in human history that greatly improved the early humans' ability to survive. [1] Coo____ food, [2] partic______ meat [3] a__ tubers, [4] ma__ digesting [5] nutr_____ much [6] eas___. Fire [7] al__ provided [8] war___ in [9] col___ climates, [10] allo____ humans to expand their geographic range and survive in areas where they might not have otherwise. In addition, fire was used to harden wood for tools like spears and to shape stones for cutting and scraping, thus contributing to advances in toolmaking.

content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: Learning the controlled use of fire was a key development in human history that greatly improved the early humans' ability to survive. [1] Coo____ food, [2] partic______ meat [3] a__ tubers, [4] ma__ digesting [5] nutr_____ much [6] eas___. Fire [7] al__ provided [8] war___ in [9] col___ climates, [10] allo____ humans to expand their geographic range and survive in areas where they might not have otherwise. In addition, fire was used to harden wood for tools like spears and to shape stones for cutting and scraping, thus contributing to advances in toolmaking.

reading.answer:
1. king → Cooking
2. ularly → particularly
3. nd → and
4. de → made
5. ients → nutrients
6. ier → easier
7. so → also
8. mth → warmth
9. der → colder
10. wing → allowing
reading.explanation: 1. 这里需要填入'Cooking'，是动词cook的现在分词，表示烹饪食物这一行为，使后文的消化营养更容易。 2. 这里需要填入'particularly'，意思是'特别地'，用于强调食物中的肉和块茎，突出这些类型。 3. 这里需要填入'and'，作为并列连词，连接'meat'和'tubers'两个名词，表示两者都包括。 4. 这里需要填入'made'，是动词make的过去式，表示使变得，后接宾语和形容词比较级，说明烹饪的效果。 5. 这里需要填入'nutrients'，意思是营养，是动词'digesting'的宾语，表示消化的对象是营养。 6. 这里需要填入'easier'，是形容词easy的比较级，与'much'连用，表示消化营养变得更容易。 7. 这里需要填入'also'，意思是'也'，表示火除了烹饪外，还有其他功能，如提供温暖。 8. 这里需要填入'warmth'，意思是温暖，是动词'provided'的宾语，表示火提供的东西。 9. 这里需要填入'colder'，是形容词cold的比较级，修饰'climates'，表示更冷的气候条件。 10. 这里需要填入'allowing'，是动词allow的现在分词，表示结果，使得人类能够扩展地理范围。
reading.translation: 学会受控用火是人类历史上的关键发展，极大提高了早期人类的生存能力。烹饪食物——尤其是肉与块茎——使消化养分容易得多。火也在较冷气候中提供温暖，使人类能扩展地理范围，并在原本可能无法生存的地区存活。此外，火被用来硬化木材以制作长矛等工具，并塑形石头用于切割与刮削，从而推动工具制造进步。

[10] I_ this skill innate or shaped by experience? Is understanding others' mental states a matter of simulation (imagining ourselves in their place) or theory (applying a set of rules or concepts)? content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: One of the topics psychologists investigate is our capacity to understand the mental states of others. This [1] abi____ is [2] funda______ for [3] soc___ interaction [4] bec____ it [5] ena____ us [6] t_ predict [7] a__ explain [8] t__ behavior [9] o_ others. [10] I_ this skill innate or shaped by experience? Is understanding others' mental states a matter of simulation (imagining ourselves in their place) or theory (applying a set of rules or concepts)? These inquiries contribute to broader discussions about human cognition.

reading.answer:
1. lity → ability
2. mental → fundamental
3. ial → social
4. ause → because
5. bles → enables
6. o → to
7. nd → and
8. he → the
9. f → of
10. s → Is
reading.explanation: 1. abi____ 补全为 ability，表示“能力”，后接不定式 to understand，符合 ability to do sth. 的固定搭配，与 capacity 呼应。 2. funda______ 补全为 fundamental，意为“基本的”，修饰 social interaction，表示这种能力对社交互动是基础性的。 3. soc___ 补全为 social，与 interaction 搭配成 social interaction，意为“社交互动”，是常见短语。 4. bec____ 补全为 because，引导原因状语从句，解释为什么这种能力是基本的。 5. ena____ 补全为 enables，表示“使能够”，后接 us to...，是 enable sb. to do sth. 的结构。 6. t_ 补全为 to，与 enables 搭配，构成 enables us to predict... 的不定式形式。 7. a__ 补全为 and，连接 predict 和 explain 两个动词，表示并列动作。 8. t__ 补全为 the，定冠词特指 behavior，指他人的行为。 9. o_ 补全为 of，表示所属关系，behavior of others 意为“他人的行为”。 10. I_ 补全为 Is，是 be 动词的第三人称单数，用于疑问句 Is this skill innate... 的开头。
reading.translation: 心理学家研究的课题之一是我们理解他人心理状态的能力。这种能力对社会互动至关重要，因为它使我们能预测并解释他人行为。这种技能是先天的，还是由经验塑造？理解他人心理状态是模拟（设想自己处在对方位置）还是理论（运用一套规则或概念）？这些追问有助于关于人类认知的更广泛讨论。

reading.title: Reactor Article
reading.prompt: All of the following are true of the new nuclear reactor EXCEPT:
reading.promptZh: 关于新型核反应堆，以下哪项描述是不正确的？
reading.passage:
Yesterday, the university flipped the switch on its new nuclear research reactor in the basement of the Franklin Applied Energy Lab, turning the engineering quad into the hottest spot on campus — literally and figuratively. The reactor, about the size of a classroom, is built for neutron experiments, advanced materials research, and isotope production. While some students have expressed safety concerns, a university spokesperson assured the community that radiation levels outside the facility are lower than what you would get on a cross-country flight. Meanwhile, the Physics Club is planning a festive "Critical Mass Mixer" for Friday evening.

Yesterday, the university flipped the switch on its new nuclear research reactor in the basement of the Franklin Applied Energy Lab, turning the engineering quad into the hottest spot on campus-literally and figuratively. The reactor, about the size of a classroom, won't charge cell phones or brew coffee; it's built for neutron experiments, advanced materials research, and isotope production. "The launch of this laboratory will provide unparalleled opportunities for the university," said Dr. Evelyn Pillai, project lead.
While some students have expressed safety concerns, a university spokesperson assured the community that the reactor is safer than the chemistry labs most first-year students wander into. "Radiation levels outside the facility are lower than what you'd get on a cross-country flight," said Dr. Pillai. Meanwhile, the Physics Club is planning a festive "Critical Mass Mixer" for Friday evening. The invitation features an atom whose colorful orbiting electrons are juggled by a mole.

reading.translation:
关于新型核反应堆，以下哪项描述是不正确的？

昨天，大学在富兰克林应用能源实验室地下室启动了新的核研究反应堆，把工程四方院变成校园最「热」的地方——字面与比喻皆然。该反应堆大约一间教室大小，不会给手机充电或煮咖啡；它为中子实验、先进材料研究与同位素生产而建。「这个实验室的启动将为大学提供无与伦比的机会，」项目负责人伊芙琳·皮莱博士说。
尽管一些学生表达安全关切，大学发言人向社区保证，该反应堆比多数一年级学生走进的化学实验室更安全。「设施外的辐射水平低于你跨大陆飞行所受到的，」皮莱博士说。与此同时，物理俱乐部计划周五晚举办喜庆的「临界质量酒会」。请柬上画着一个原子，彩色电子被一只鼹鼠抛接。

昨天，大学在富兰克林应用能源实验室地下室启动了新的核研究反应堆，把工程四方院变成校园最「热」的地方——字面与比喻皆然。该反应堆大约一间教室大小，不会给手机充电或煮咖啡；它为中子实验、先进材料研究与同位素生产而建。「这个实验室的启动将为大学提供无与伦比的机会，」项目负责人伊芙琳·皮莱博士说。
尽管一些学生表达安全关切，大学发言人向社区保证，该反应堆比多数一年级学生走进的化学实验室更安全。「设施外的辐射水平低于你跨大陆飞行所受到的，」皮莱博士说。与此同时，物理俱乐部计划周五晚举办喜庆的「临界质量酒会」。请柬上画着一个原子，彩色电子被一只鼹鼠抛接。

reading.title: A Unique Advantage of Spicy Cuisine
reading.prompt: What is the purpose of the passage?
reading.promptZh: 这篇文章的目的是什么？
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Are you fond of spicy food? Spices have been used for thousands of years to enhance the flavor of food, originally in cultures where spice plants were native to the area. Today, spice use is widespread across cultures, though certain spices are more prevalent in some cuisines. Indeed, scientists have suggested that hot-climate cuisines feature a greater amount and variety of spices. For example, a recent study found that the number of different spices was much greater in traditional recipes from Southeast Asian countries than in those from northern Europe.

Paragraph 2
Why do hot-climate cuisines feature more spices? Some believe that spice consumption is related to cultural preferences. While culture certainly plays a part, scientists have recently suggested that the antimicrobial properties of spices, which prevent the growth of dangerous foodborne microorganisms, ensured their widespread use in hot climates. In such climates, food spoilage was a concern before the availability of refrigeration. Spices with greater antimicrobial or antibacterial properties, such as allspice, cinnamon, cumin, garlic, and onions, were frequently featured in the traditional recipes of hot-climate cuisines and in different combinations. Scientists concluded that food safety precipitated the use of many and multiple spices in hot regions.

reading.translation:
这篇文章的目的是什么？

你喜欢辛辣食物吗？香料被用于增强食物风味已有数千年，最初出现在香料植物原产地的文化中。如今香料使用跨文化普及，但某些香料在特定菜系中更常见。确实，科学家提出：炎热气候的菜系使用的香料数量与种类更多。例如，一项近期研究发现，东南亚国家传统食谱中不同香料的数量远多于北欧食谱。
为何炎热气候菜系更爱用香料？有人认为这与文化偏好有关。文化固然重要，但科学家近年提出：香料的抗菌特性——抑制危险食源性微生物——促成了其在炎热气候的广泛使用。在冷藏普及前，这类气候中食物腐败是大问题。抗菌或抑菌能力较强的香料，如多香果、肉桂、孜然、大蒜与洋葱，在炎热地区传统食谱中频繁出现并以不同组合使用。科学家据此认为，食品安全推动了炎热地区多用、并用多种香料。

你喜欢辛辣食物吗？香料被用于增强食物风味已有数千年，最初出现在香料植物原产地的文化中。如今香料使用跨文化普及，但某些香料在特定菜系中更常见。确实，科学家提出：炎热气候的菜系使用的香料数量与种类更多。例如，一项近期研究发现，东南亚国家传统食谱中不同香料的数量远多于北欧食谱。
为何炎热气候菜系更爱用香料？有人认为这与文化偏好有关。文化固然重要，但科学家近年提出：香料的抗菌特性——抑制危险食源性微生物——促成了其在炎热气候的广泛使用。在冷藏普及前，这类气候中食物腐败是大问题。抗菌或抑菌能力较强的香料，如多香果、肉桂、孜然、大蒜与洋葱，在炎热地区传统食谱中频繁出现并以不同组合使用。科学家据此认为，食品安全推动了炎热地区多用、并用多种香料。

He [1] i_ best [2] kn___ for [3] h__ three [4] voy____ across [5] t__ Pacific [6] Oc___, during [7] wh___ he [8] meticu______ mapped [9] coast_____ and [10] coll_____ data on astronomy, natural history, and oceanography. reading.answer:
1. s → is
2. own → known
3. is → his
4. ages → voyages
5. he → the
6. ean → Ocean
7. ich → which
8. lously → meticulously
9. lines → coastlines
10. ected → collected
reading.explanation: 1. 因为'British'是表示国籍的形容词，拼写需要's'来完成单词。 2. 'best known for'是固定短语，意为'因...而著名'，需要'own'来组成'known'。 3. 'his'是物主代词，指'他的'，在句子中修饰名词'voyages'，所以填'is'完成'his'。 4. 'voyages'是名词，意为'航行'，与前面的'three'和介词'across'搭配，需要'ages'来完成单词。 5. 'the'是定冠词，特指'Pacific Ocean'，所以需要'he'来组成'the'。 6. 'Ocean'是专有名词'Pacific Ocean'的一部分，表示海洋，拼写需要'ean'。 7. 'which'引导非限制性定语从句，修饰前面的整个句子，解释Cook的行为，需要'ich'来完成单词。 8. 'meticulously'是副词，意为'细致地'，修饰动词'mapped'，表示Cook绘制地图的方式，需要'lously'来完成单词。 9. 'coastlines'是名词，意为'海岸线'，是'mapped'的宾语，需要'lines'来完成单词。 10. 'collected'是动词，意为'收集'，与'coll'前缀和'data'搭配，需要'ected'来完成单词。
reading.translation: 詹姆斯·库克是 1728 年出生的英国海军军官、探险家与制图师。他以三次横跨太平洋的航行最著名，其间细致绘制海岸线，并收集天文学、博物学与海洋学数据。库克是第一个环航新西兰并接触夏威夷群岛的欧洲人。他也因在船上实施健康措施而著称，例如通过饮食改变预防坏血病。

reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Urban green spaces, such as parks and community gardens, enhance city life for residents. The contrast between green spaces and the surrounding concrete and glass structures can be a visual respite; such spaces also provide residents with a place to relax and connect with nature, which can significantly improve mental health, reduce stress, and encourage physical activity.

Paragraph 2
Urban green spaces also contribute to environmental sustainability. They provide a cooler spot within the concrete heat traps surrounding them, absorb rainwater and reduce flooding, and increase biodiversity by providing habitats for various species.

Paragraph 3
Recent initiatives have focused on creating more green spaces in underserved areas. Some cities are converting abandoned lots into community gardens or small parks. These projects not only provide green spaces but also involve community members in the planning and maintenance of them, fostering a sense of ownership and responsibility.

Paragraph 4
While urban green spaces offer a host of benefits, they are not without drawbacks. When parks and gardens are added in city neighborhoods, they often increase the value of nearby properties. This can unintentionally lead to the displacement of longtime residents who can no longer afford rising rents or property taxes. Another challenge is preserving these spaces—it can be difficult to secure the funding necessary to maintain them.

reading.translation:
文中单词"respite"最接近以下哪个意思？

公园与社区花园等城市绿地改善了居民的城市生活。绿地与周围混凝土、玻璃建筑的对比可带来视觉放松；它们也提供休憩与亲近自然的场所，显著改善心理健康、减轻压力并鼓励身体活动。
城市绿地也有助于环境可持续性。它们在混凝土热岛中形成凉爽点，吸收雨水、减轻洪涝，并为多种物种提供栖息地以增加生物多样性。
近期倡议聚焦在服务不足地区建设更多绿地。一些城市把废弃地块改成社区花园或小公园。这些项目不仅提供绿地，还让社区成员参与规划与维护，培养主人翁意识与责任感。
虽有诸多益处，城市绿地也非没有弊端。在社区增设公园花园往往会推高附近房价，可能无意中迫使无力承担上涨租金或房产税的老住户迁离。另一挑战是维护：筹集资金持续保养这些空间往往困难。

reading.promptZh: 文中四个位置可以添加以下句子："有些甚至整合了游乐场、运动场和健身站，使此类活动对当地居民既便捷又有趣。" 句子最适合放在哪里？
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Urban green spaces, such as parks and community gardens, enhance city life for residents. The contrast between green spaces and the surrounding concrete and glass structures can be a visual respite; such spaces also provide residents with a place to relax and connect with nature, which can significantly improve mental health, reduce stress, and encourage physical activity. 【位置 1】

Paragraph 2
Urban green spaces also contribute to environmental sustainability. 【位置 2】 They provide a cooler spot within the concrete heat traps surrounding them, absorb rainwater and reduce flooding, and increase biodiversity by providing habitats for various species. 【位置 3】

Paragraph 3
Recent initiatives have focused on creating more green spaces in underserved areas. 【位置 4】 Some cities are converting abandoned lots into community gardens or small parks. These projects not only provide green spaces but also involve community members in the planning and maintenance of them, fostering a sense of ownership and responsibility.

Paragraph 4
While urban green spaces offer a host of benefits, they are not without drawbacks. When parks and gardens are added in city neighborhoods, they often increase the value of nearby properties. This can unintentionally lead to the displacement of longtime residents who can no longer afford rising rents or property taxes. Another challenge is preserving these spaces—it can be difficult to secure the funding necessary to maintain them.

reading.translation:
文中四个位置可以添加以下句子："有些甚至整合了游乐场、运动场和健身站，使此类活动对当地居民既便捷又有趣。" 句子最适合放在哪里？

公园与社区花园等城市绿地改善了居民的城市生活。绿地与周围混凝土、玻璃建筑的对比可带来视觉放松；它们也提供休憩与亲近自然的场所，显著改善心理健康、减轻压力并鼓励身体活动。
城市绿地也有助于环境可持续性。它们在混凝土热岛中形成凉爽点，吸收雨水、减轻洪涝，并为多种物种提供栖息地以增加生物多样性。
近期倡议聚焦在服务不足地区建设更多绿地。一些城市把废弃地块改成社区花园或小公园。这些项目不仅提供绿地，还让社区成员参与规划与维护，培养主人翁意识与责任感。
虽有诸多益处，城市绿地也非没有弊端。在社区增设公园花园往往会推高附近房价，可能无意中迫使无力承担上涨租金或房产税的老住户迁离。另一挑战是维护：筹集资金持续保养这些空间往往困难。

listening.translation: 这个讲座主要关于什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a history class. 
The Age of Exploration extended from the 15th century to the 17th century, but long before this, seafarers were venturing into unfamiliar waters using remarkably sophisticated techniques. One notable example is Pytheas of Massalia, a Greek explorer from the 4th century BCE. He sailed from the Mediterranean to the northern reaches of Europe, possibly reaching Britain and even Iceland. Without modern instruments, Pytheas relied on coastal landmarks, the position of the sun and stars, and careful observation of ocean tides and daylight patterns. His journey demonstrated that long-distance navigation was possible through keen environmental awareness and methodical planning. Centuries later, European explorers expanded on these early achievements with the help of new technologies. Among the most transformative was the magnetic compass, which used a magnetized needle to indicate direction. Originally developed in China and later adopted in Europe, the compass allowed sailors to maintain a heading even when celestial bodies were obscured by clouds or fog. This innovation enabled mariners to venture into open seas with greater confidence and precision. Historians note that the compass didn't just improve navigation; it transformed it. It allowed explorers like Vasco da Gama and Ferdinand Magellan to chart new maritime routes across vast oceans, connecting continents and reshaping global trade. Combined with other tools like the astrolabe and improved ship designs, the compass helped usher in the Age of Exploration.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段历史课的讲座。
大航海时代从十五世纪延伸到十七世纪，但在此之前很久，航海者就用极为精密的技术驶入陌生水域。一个显著例子是马萨利亚的皮西亚斯，公元前四世纪的希腊探险家。他从地中海航行到欧洲北部，可能到达不列颠甚至冰岛。没有现代仪器，皮西亚斯依靠海岸地标、日月星辰位置，以及对海潮与日照模式的仔细观察。他的旅程证明，通过敏锐的环境意识与有条不紊的计划，长距离导航是可能的。数世纪后，欧洲探险家借助新技术扩展了这些早期成就。最具变革性的之一是磁罗盘，用磁化指针指示方向。罗盘原产中国、后被欧洲采用，使水手即使在云雾遮蔽天体时也能保持航向。这一创新使航海者能更自信、更精确地驶入公海。历史学家指出，罗盘不只改进了导航；它改变了导航。它使瓦斯科·达·伽马与费迪南德·麦哲伦等探险家能在浩瀚大洋上开辟新航线，连接大陆并重塑全球贸易。结合星盘等其他工具与改进的船舶设计，罗盘帮助开启了大航海时代。
